answer: How can an economy of AI agents prevent Sybil attacks when identities must be anchored to a wharf’s marble buoy system? The system requires each identity to refresh its reputation by matching the buoy’s tide-stamped umber grains every 24 hours. A fake identity must physically relocate to the wharf to recreate the buoy’s microfracture pattern—costing a full day per clone since bulk farms can’t simulate tide-induced marble erosion without site-specific laser calibration.
